[00:00] Maya Chen: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, we know you're busy so we'll try to keep this tight. I'm Maya, AE on this engagement, with Aaron and Diego. who do we have from BrightMarsh?

[00:26] Tom Keller: yep that's right. the main ask from our side is we want to validate latency at p95 under 200ms for the smallest model we plan to use and understand cost implications.
[00:36] Diego Ramos: got it. we'll propose a Dedicated pool for the pilot but we can also run hosted to compare. for latency benchmarking we'll need representative prompts — Hannah can share samples?
[00:45] Hannah Li: yes I'll put together a 300-message sample set, mixture of short routing queries and longer parse jobs.
[00:52] Aaron Patel: and from an ops perspective we'll provide a staging workspace, or if you prefer a private deployment we'll walk through credentials. what is your networking posture?
[01:02] Jon Park: we prefer VPC peering to keep traffic internal, egress rules are strict — only specific subnets and SGs allowed.
[01:10] Rita Singh: also want to ensure customer-managed KMS; we can't hand over raw data to external keys. additionally SOC2 requirements — we'll need audit log access.
[01:21] Maya Chen: understood. Redwood Private supports customer KMS and audit logs. there are a couple of options: VPC peering into our control plane or a Private VPC deployment. Diego, maybe you can give a quick outline of the typical network patterns?
[01:33] Diego Ramos: sure. most customers either use a peered control plane with TLS over private link or run the on-prem bundle behind a firewall. for peering we'll need a few items: CIDR ranges, NAT/egress info, and an account owner for the peering tunnel. sometimes hostnames get weird in the transcription — sorry, i mean we'll exchange the exact details.
[01:53] Tom Keller: for the peering tunnel, we'll need concrete docs so our infra team can approve. can you send the network diagram?
[02:02] Maya Chen: yes that's on the runbook I'll share after the call. link in next steps.
[02:08] Sonia Alvarez: timeline — we want pilot started within two weeks if possible, is that feasible?
[02:14] Aaron Patel: yes, two weeks is doable. the critical path is network approvals and KMS. if Tom and Rita can provide the CIDRs and KMS policy we'll start provisioning.
[02:24] Rita Singh: quick Q — are token logs redacted? we need to ensure PII isn't stored unencrypted.
[02:30] Diego Ramos: we have configurable retention and can disable raw transcript retention for the pilot. audit logs are separated and can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[02:40] Jon Park: what about SSO? we want SAML + SCIM for user provisioning.
[02:46] Lina Park: we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; we'll include the SSO guide in the runbook.
[02:52] Hannah Li: for the benchmark data, do you need tokenized counts or raw text?
[02:56] Diego Ramos: raw text is fine, we'll measure tokenization on our side; send the raw samples and an expected traffic shape.
[03:04] Maya Chen: ok starting to map milestones — Day 0 share runbook + network diagram, Day 2 get CIDRs and KMS policy, Day 5 staging access and sample ingestion, Week 2 benchmark window and initial results.
[03:18] Tom Keller: can you put those milestones into a calendar invite?
[03:22] Maya Chen: yes will create a timeline doc and invite.
[03:26] Sonia Alvarez: do you have any red flags around volume? right now we'll route a fraction of traffic to the pilot, maybe 10%.
[03:33] Aaron Patel: 10% is a typical approach — gives us traffic to observe and keeps blast radius small. Diego will help size the Dedicated pool if you want reserved capacity.
[03:43] Diego Ramos: one note — batching settings and KV cache behavior impact latency. for the routing use-case small messages mean batching is low; we'll tune batch targets to prioritize latency not throughput.
[03:55] Jon Park: are there default quotas we should expect? burst capacity?
[03:59] Aaron Patel: yes, for Dedicated we can set burst extents, and for hosted we have soft limits. we'll include an example config.
[04:07] Rita Singh: audit — how granular are logs? we need per-token and per-request logs for compliance.
[04:12] Diego Ramos: we capture request metadata, IP, model/route, and token counts; redaction can be enabled. full transcript capture is optional.
[04:21] Hannah Li: okay for the sample prompts, some are longer — doc parsing one is like 600 tokens. will that affect the latency numbers?
[04:28] Diego Ramos: yes long sequences raise generation time; we'll run both short and long path benchmarks and show per-length p50/p95.
[04:35] Maya Chen: quick practical: Diego will run two benchmark modes — small prompt routing and doc-parse; we'll share the runbook and sample ingestion steps.
[04:44] Tom Keller: context about billing: can you share an estimate for the pilot (50% traffic scenario)?
[04:50] Aaron Patel: we'll model cost based on token usage and Dedicated pool hours — I'll prepare a conservative estimate and an aggressive one.
[04:57] Sonia Alvarez: favorite question — backups and retention policy for models and cache?
[05:01] Lina Park: model artifacts are versioned; KV caches are ephemeral but can be checkpointed if you need. retention policies are configurable.
[05:08] Jon Park: curious about fallbacks — if Dedicated pool is unavailable what's the failover?
[05:13] Diego Ramos: we recommend a fallback route to hosted variants or a smaller quantized model; that'll be in the rollout plan.
[05:20] Rita Singh: any SOC2 or ISO certs you can share?
[05:23] Maya Chen: yes we'll attach our security pack, SOC2 Type II report and network diagrams to the runbook link.
[05:30] Hannah Li: regarding data residency — we need to keep EU data in the EU region. is there a region pinning option?
[05:36] Diego Ramos: yes region pinning is supported; the control plane is agnostic but data path can be pinned to EU-only infra. we'll document that.
[05:44] Maya Chen: ok shifting to ops handoff — Lina will own the runbook maintenance and Aaron is primary CSM. Lina, you want to summarize the immediate next actions?
[05:52] Lina Park: sure: I'll update the runbook with a network checklist and SSO instructions. Diego will draft the benchmark plan. Aaron will pull together cost scenarios. Maya will send the runbook link and invite.
[06:04] Tom Keller: we may need a security deep-dive — Rita, can you say what you'd like in that session?
[06:10] Rita Singh: we'll want KMS integration details, key rotation policy, data retention controls, and an audit log delivery method. also SLA and incident response expectations.
[06:21] Aaron Patel: we'll prep those items and propose a 45-min Security Deep Dive next week if that works.

[06:42] Jon Park: one last thing — do you offer any automated caching for common prefixes? that's useful for our routing flows.
[06:48] Diego Ramos: yes we have prefix/KV caching; we'll show cache hit stats in the dashboard.
[06:54] Maya Chen: ok wrapping up. I'll read back next steps.
